title: Shallow Alignment After Domain Fine-Tuning: Does Medical QA Fine-Tuning Deepen or Erode First-Token Safety?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: medical domain fine-tuning of open-weight models is widespread. If it disproportionately erodes the first-token safety shortcut, this reveals a gap between current safety evaluations and real deployments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires fine-tuning Llama-3-8B (even on 500 examples needs LoRA/QLoRA setup), understanding prefilling attacks, and measuring token-level alignment distribution. Exceeds beginner CS student capabilities without significant mentoring.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: fine-tuning pipeline setup, before/after measurement at multiple token positions, prefilling attack implementation, and analysis of spatial alignment degradation. Multiple stages each requiring debugging.

evidence: Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' establishes shallow alignment as concentrated in first few tokens and shows fine-tuning erodes it.
Re-Emergent Misalignment (arXiv:2507.03662) demonstrates that narrow domain fine-tuning causes broad, domain-agnostic safety erosion.
Multiple papers (2024-2025) confirm fine-tuning even on benign data degrades safety alignment.

The specific angle of measuring first-token concentration changes after medical QA fine-tuning is a specific instantiation of well-characterized phenomena, though the medical domain focus and token-level spatial analysis adds some specificity.
